|Instruction|rd is x0|rs1 is x0|Reads CSR|Writes CSR|
|CSRRW|Yes|-|No|Yes|
|CSRRW|No|-|Yes|Yes|
|CSRRS/CSRRC|-|Yes|Yes|No|

grades.reason: The table directly establishes that CSRRS suppresses writes only when rs1 names x0; another register causes a write even if its value is zero.
The vector strcmp example does not explain CSRRS write behavior.

grades.quote: For both CSRRS and CSRRC, if _rs1_ = `x0` , then the instruction will not write to the CSR at all, and so shall not cause any of the side effects that might otherwise occur on a CSR write, nor raise illegalinstruction exceptions on accesses to read-only CSRs. Both CSRRS and CSRRC always read the addressed CSR and cause any read side effects regardless of _rs1_ and _rd_ fields. Note that if _rs1_ specifies a register other than `x0` , and that register holds a zero value, the instruction will not action any attendant per-field side effects, but will action any side effects caused by writing to the entire CSR.
grades.reason: Explicitly contrasts x0, which suppresses the write, with another zero-valued register, which still triggers whole-CSR write side effects but not per-field side effects.
